answer: Every head needs an unrelated whisper to stake opals behind it in the shrine before it may trade, and no whisper stakes twice. The atlas records every vow and the opals behind it. Each further head of an operator needs its own whisper, and that whisper must lock the pool the atlas records for that operator, so the pool doubles with every head, and a whisper that finds two of that operator's heads in the atlas to be copies forfeits its opals to the shrine. So the k-th head of one operator costs a fresh whisper and 2^(k-1) opals; a single first agent needs one whisper and one opal.
